title: The Hotelier’s Guide to Agentic AI for Hospitality
summary: Learn what agentic AI for hospitality is, how AI agents work across the guest journey, and how to prepare your hotel for adoption—without the risk.
body_text: AI in the hospitality industry has moved beyond simple chatbots and content generation. Now, hoteliers are turning their focus toward Agentic AI for hospitality — the next major tech evolution that gets work done for you. Instead of answering questions or drafting text, AI agents complete entire tasks, from confirming a booking change to routing a maintenance request to the right person on your team. This guide breaks down what the technology actually is, how it works, where it fits across your operation and how to prepare your hotel for adoption without putting the guest experience at risk. Key highlights: Agentic AI for hospitality is software that uses AI agents to plan and complete hotel tasks on their own, working across your connected systems. Traditional automation follows fixed rules and generative AI creates content, while AI agents decide, act and follow up. Hotels put AI agents to work on reservations, guest communication, front desk support, phone calls and post-stay engagement. Canary Technologies builds AI agents specifically for hotels, trained on hospitality workflows and plugged into the systems your team already uses. What Are AI Agents for Hospitality? AI agents for hospitality are software programs that can understand a request, make a plan and carry it out across your hotel’s systems without a staff member driving every step. While a chatbot just answers a question and a writing assistant drafts an email, an agent works through each step until the job is done or a human needs to weigh in. Give it a goal, like “confirm this guest’s late checkout and update housekeeping,” and it gets to work. In a hotel context, agents are built for hospitality rather than generic business software. They understand what a folio is. They know the difference between a booking modification and a cancellation. And they connect directly to your property management system, so their answers reflect what’s actually happening at your property rather than a generic script. How Does an AI Agent for Hotels Work? An AI agent for hotels works in a loop: take in a request, figure out what needs to happen, then go do it. While it’s simple to describe, it’s genuinely hard to build, which is why the technology has only recently become practical for hotels of every size. Here’s what that loop looks like in practice: Receive a Guest Request or Operational Goal: The starting point can be a guest text asking about parking, a phone call about a reservation or an internal trigger like a room going out of order. Interpret the Request and Relevant Context: The agent reads intent, not just keywords. A guest who asks, “Can we get in early?” now has an early check-in request tied to their specific booking. Identify the Actions Required: It maps out the steps. An early check-in request might mean checking Friday’s arrivals, confirming room availability and applying a fee if your policy calls for one. Access Connected Hotel Systems and Information: The agent pulls live data from your Property Management System (PMS), your knowledge base and your policies. Complete the Task or Route It to the Appropriate Staff: If the task falls within its guardrails, the agent completes the job and confirms with the guest. If not, it hands everything to your team with full context attached. Monitor the Outcome and Adjust When Necessary: Good agents check their work. If a guest replies with a follow-up or something changes in the system, the agent picks the thread back up. How Agentic AI Differs from Generative AI and Traditional Automation These three terms are often used interchangeably, and the confusion costs hoteliers real money when they buy one expecting the other. AI agents for hospitality sit at the top of a capability ladder. Traditional automation is the bottom rung and generative AI is the middle. Agents combine the reliability of the first with the intelligence of the second, plus the ability to act. Comparison Points Traditional Automation Generative AI Agentic AI for Hospitality Primary Purpose Repeat a fixed task the same way every time Create content: text, replies or summaries Complete goals from start to finish How It Operates If-this-then-that rules are set up in advance Responds to prompts one at a time Plans multi-step work and adapts as it goes Level of Autonomy None, it only fires when triggered Low — a person drives every exchange High, it works independently within set guardrails Decision-Making Ability Cannot handle exceptions Suggests options but doesn’t choose Weighs context and picks the next step System Interaction Usually limited to one system None — it works in a chat window Reads and writes across PMS, messaging and payment tools Human Involvement Setup and constant maintenance Hands-on for every task Oversight, exceptions and approvals How Hotels Use AI Agents Across the Guest Journey The best way to understand agentic AI for hospitality is to consider the entire stay. From the moment a traveler researches their options to the review they leave after checkout, there are dozens of small tasks that eat up your team’s time. Agents can take on most of them. 1. Reservation Management and Direct Bookings Travelers increasingly expect to book the way they message: instantly, conversationally and at midnight. The TravelBoom 2026 Leisure Travel Study found that 83% of travelers already use or want to use AI tools to plan their trips. If your website can’t answer “do you have a king room with a bathtub next weekend” in real time, that booking often drifts to an online travel agency (OTA) that can. A hotel AI chatbot with agentic capabilities changes that outcome. It can: Answer availability questions with live rates and room types pulled straight from your systems. Handle modifications like date changes, room upgrades and cancelations without a phone call. Rescue abandoned bookings by following up with travelers who started but never finished a reservation. 2. Pre-Arrival Communication The window between booking and check-in is where great stays are set up — agents use this time to enhance the guest experience without adding to anyone’s workload. Strong pre-arrival guest communication handled by an agent confirms arrival times, collects preferences, answers the check-in questions before they hit your inbox and offers early check-in or room upgrades while the guest is still excited about the trip. 3. Guest Messaging and Concierge Support During the stay, agents become a tireless concierge. Connected to your guest messaging platform, they answer text or emailed questions about WiFi passwords, pool hours and dinner recommendations in seconds — and in the guest’s own language. The quiet win here is triage. The agent handles routine tasks on its own and flags messages that actually need a staff member, like a complaint about a noisy neighbor, so your team spends time where it matters. 4. Front Desk and On-Property Operations Your front desk handles an enormous amount of administrative work, which can distract staff from interacting with guests. Agents can reduce front desk friction by taking over the paperwork. When managing hotel guest information updates, AI agents verify details, correct a misspelled name on a reservation, update contact information and sync those changes across systems so your staff isn’t retyping the same data three times. They can also collect registration details and payment information before the guest ever reaches the lobby. 5. AI Voice Support The phone still matters in hotels. It’s also likely to go unanswered at 2 p.m. on a Saturday when the desk has a line five deep. An AI voice agent for hospitality businesses answers every call on the first ring, handles the common questions and books reservations over the phone. AI voice technology built for hotels knows when to transfer. A caller asking about checkout time doesn’t need a human. A caller with a billing dispute always does. Good voice agents can tell the difference and route accordingly. 6. Guest Information and Post-Stay Engagement Checkout is actually the beginning of the next hotel guest journey . Agents follow up with thank-you messages, request reviews while the stay is fresh, respond to feedback and re-engage past guests with offers tailored to what they booked last time. That’s the kind of consistent follow-through most teams intend to do and never quite find time for. Benefits of AI Agents for Hotels Adoption of agentic AI is racing ahead of execution. A 2026 Wyndham Hotels & Resorts survey found that 98% of hotel owners have started using AI in some form, yet only 32% say it’s embedded across most of their operations. In other words, nearly everyone is experimenting and very few are realizing the technology’s full value. Agents are how hotels close that gap, because they turn scattered AI experiments into finished work. Here’s what AI agents for hotels deliver when they’re set up well: Reducing Repetitive Work: Confirmation emails, standard questions, data entry and routine updates disappear from your team’s to-do list, freeing hours every shift for actual guest service. Providing Faster Guest Responses: Guests get answers in seconds, at any hour and in any language, instead of waiting for the desk to clear. Improving Departmental Coordination: When a guest reports a broken AC, the agent logs the ticket, notifies engineering and updates the guest when it’s fixed. Personalizing Guest Interactions: With AI guest messaging , responses draw on the guest’s history and preferences, so a returning guest gets treated like one. Capturing Upsell Opportunities : Agents offer the right upgrade to the right guest at the right moment, like late checkout on a Sunday or a suite upgrade for an anniversary stay. How Should Hotels Prepare for Agentic AI? Hotels should prepare for agentic AI by starting with their most painful workflows, cleaning up their data and setting clear rules for what agents can and can’t do on their own. You don’t need a task force or a six-month rollout plan. You do need a deliberate approach, and here's how: 1. Identify High-Impact Workflows Start where the pain is loudest. Sit with your front desk for an afternoon and count how many times they answer the same five questions. Pull your call logs. Check how many bookings abandon at the payment step. The best first workflows share three traits: they’re frequent, they’re repetitive and getting them wrong is low-risk. Answering “What time is breakfast?” fits; handling a chargeback dispute doesn’t, at least not yet. 2. Connect Hotel Systems and Data An agent is only as smart as the data it can reach. If your PMS, messaging platform and payment tools don’t talk to each other, the agent ends up guessing, and guessing is where AI gets embarrassing. Before rollout, audit your integrations and your knowledge base. Are your policies written down anywhere, and are they current? Is the parking fee on your website the same one your desk actually charges? Fix those gaps first. Agents amplify whatever information you feed them, accurate or not. 3. Establish Guardrails and Escalation Paths Decide upfront what the agent can do on its own, what needs approval and what always goes to staff. Write it down. Then build the escalation path so handoffs carry context, because nothing frustrates a guest like repeating their problem to a person after explaining it to a bot. Sensible starting guardrails include: Autonomous: FAQs, booking confirmations, routine updates and standard upsell offers. Approval required: Refunds, rate exceptions and policy overrides. Always human: Complaints, emergencies and anything involving a distressed guest. 4. Preserve Brand and Service Standards Guests should feel your hotel’s personality in every interaction, automated or not. Train the agent on your voice, your standards and your service recovery playbook, and review its conversations regularly as you’d review a new hire’s. Hoteliers themselves are clear-eyed about the limits here: agents should protect the human moments, not replace them, and pairing them with hotel reputation management tools makes sure the guest experience is actually improving as automation expands. 5. Start Small and Measure Results Pick one workflow. Run it for 30 days. Measure response times, resolution rates, staff hours saved and guest satisfaction before and after. Then expand to the next workflow with real evidence behind the decision. This approach builds staff trust, too. Teams that watch an agent handle the boring stuff well become your biggest advocates for giving it more. Teams that get an ineffective tool dumped on them in week one never get on board. What Should You Look for in an Agentic AI Hospitality Platform? Look for a platform that was built for hotels, connects deeply to your existing systems and keeps staff in control of the moments that matter. Plenty of vendors have bolted the word “agent” onto a basic chatbot this year, so it pays to evaluate carefully. Use this table as your checklist: Key Features of Agentic AI for Hospitality Why It Matters What to Evaluate Technology designed specifically for hospitality Generic AI doesn’t understand folios, room blocks or the rhythm of a hotel day like hotel management software does. Ask for hotel case studies, not generic enterprise ones. Check whether training data includes real hospitality workflows. Customizable workflows and AI agent roles Your agents shouldn’t be generic. A configurable hospitality AI agent adapts to your policies and brand voice. What each agent handles and if you can adjust its tone and change its rules without a developer. Multichannel communication capabilities Guests move between text, WhatsApp, web chat, email and phone. A truly helpful agent is available everywhere. Confirm that the agent keeps context when a guest switches channels mid-conversation. Human oversight and escalation controls Autonomy without guardrails is a liability. You need visibility into what agents are doing and a fast way to step in. Review the escalation setup, approval workflows and conversation logs before you buy. Reporting tied to operational, revenue and guest experience outcomes If you can’t measure it, you can’t defend the spend. Agent activity should align with the metrics your hotel revenue management teams track. Look for dashboards covering resolution rates, upsell revenue, response times and satisfaction scores. Build Smarter Hotel Workflows with Canary AI Canary was built for hotels from the start, which is exactly what you want in an AI partner. Canary AI Solutions power guest communication for thousands of properties worldwide, from independent boutiques to global brands, with agents trained on real hospitality conversations rather than generic text. With Canary, your property gets: AI messaging that resolves most routine guest questions instantly, in over 100 languages, across text, WhatsApp, web chat and email. A voice agent that answers every call, books reservations by phone and transfers to your team the moment a conversation needs a human. Smart upsells that surface upgrades and add-ons at the moments guests are most likely to say “yes.” Deep PMS integrations so agents act on live reservation data instead of scripts. Built-in guardrails and escalation that keep your team in control of every sensitive interaction. Book a demo today and see how Canary’s agentic AI for hospitality can automate your hotel’s guest communications, improve operations and deliver more personalized service. Frequently Asked Questions What operational tasks can agentic AI handle at my property? Quite a lot, and the list keeps growing. Today’s agents reliably handle guest FAQs, booking confirmations and modifications, pre-arrival outreach, upsell offers, review requests and routing of service tickets to the right department. On the revenue side, agents that engage website visitors in real time can help you increase direct bookings by answering the questions that would otherwise send travelers back to the OTAs. Will agentic AI make my hotel feel impersonal or replace my front desk team? Not if you deploy it well. Agents take the administrative load, which frees your team for the parts of front desk operations that actually require warmth and judgment: welcoming guests, solving problems and creating the moments people remember. Most hoteliers see it the same way, which is why the industry consensus is that arrival moments should stay human-led while agents work behind the scenes. How can AI agents optimize guest messaging? Three ways: speed (it answers in seconds), consistency (its answers always reflect your policies), and prioritization (it answers routine questions and escalates complicated conversations with full context attached). How can hotels protect guest data when using agentic AI? Choose platforms with hospitality-grade security: encryption in transit and at rest, PCI compliance for payments and clear data retention policies. Tools like secure digital authorizations show what this looks like in practice, replacing faxed credit card forms with encrypted, compliant workflows. Also confirm your vendor doesn’t train public models on your guest data. What ROI can hotels expect from agentic AI? It depends on where you deploy first, but the returns typically show up in three places: staff hours saved on repetitive work, revenue gains from consistent upselling and recovered bookings and better review scores from faster responses. Measure a baseline before launch, then track resolution rates, upsell revenue and response times monthly so the numbers make the case for you. Can small or independent operations use AI agents for hotels? Yes, and in some ways they benefit most. A 40-room independent doesn’t have a night team or an overflow call center, so an agent that answers every message and call is the closest thing to adding staff without adding payroll. Modern platforms are cloud-based with no hardware to install, and pricing scales with property size, so the technology that was once reserved for big brands is now within reach for nearly everyone.

title: Why buyer intent tracking breaks in enterprise revenue
summary: Enterprise teams have plenty of intent data, so why doesn't it convert? See where buyer intent tracking breaks down and how to fix it.
body_text: Article overview Enterprise intent breakdowns cluster around three points: scale, buying-committee size, and system fragmentation. Gartner puts the average enterprise buying committee at 11 stakeholders, which defeats single, account-level scores. The fix isn't more signal volume, it's resolution, automated scoring, and system integration. A simple ratio, accounts flagged versus accounts actually contacted with relevant context, reveals whether the fix is working. Introduction It's a familiar pattern in large revenue orgs: the intent platform shows dozens of accounts lighting up every week, the quarterly business review cites the growing signal volume as a program success, and pipeline generated from those specific flagged accounts stays flat, quarter over quarter, regardless of how much the signal count grows. Somewhere between "we have more data than ever" and "the numbers still aren't moving," the whole exercise breaks down, and it breaks down in the same three places almost every time. It's not a data problem, it's a resolution problem Enterprise teams rarely lack intent data. Most have several sources already: an ABM platform, website analytics, a data enrichment tool, maybe a dedicated intent vendor layered on top of all of it. The problem isn't volume. It's that none of these sources resolve down to an action a rep can take today, before the signal goes cold. Break point 1: scale outpaces manual triage At enterprise volume, dozens or hundreds of accounts can show some form of intent signal in a given week. Without automated scoring and prioritization, a rep or ops analyst is left manually triaging a growing queue, and triage capacity doesn't scale the way signal volume does. Signals stack up faster than a human team can review them, which is exactly the setup that produces the well-documented gap where organizations collect far more buyer signal data than they ever operationalize. Break point 2: committee size defeats account-level scoring An account-level score treats an entire buying group as a single unit. But Gartner's research on B2B buying puts the average enterprise buying committee at 11 stakeholders, and separate Gartner findings on complex purchases cite six to ten distinct decision-makers as typical. A single account score can't distinguish between an economic buyer who's ready to move and a technical evaluator who's still in early research. Only contact-level resolution can, and without it, every account-level "hot" flag is really a blended average masking who's actually ready. Break point 3: fragmented systems lose context Enterprise intent data frequently lives apart from the CRM, the call recording platform, and email history. A rep trying to act on a signal has to manually check multiple systems to understand whether the account has a closed-lost history, an existing champion, or prior sales conversations, context that should inform whether and how to reach out. That manual reconciliation is exactly where signals die before they become outreach, because most reps simply don't have 20 minutes to spend investigating every flagged account. What fixes each break point Scale requires automated scoring that runs continuously, not a periodic manual review squeezed in between calls. Committee size requires contact-level resolution, a named person and a specific reason, not an account-level flag averaged across eleven different people. Fragmentation requires a system that ingests CRM, call transcript, and signal data together rather than treating them as separate inputs a rep has to reconcile by hand. UserGems is the AI command center for outbound and ABM, built to address all three. Its Data Agents continuously capture signals, contact and account intent, job changes, buying-committee activity, and pull in your existing CRM, call transcript, and email context. Its Intelligence Agents score the resulting contacts against your own sales history and route the output automatically, a drafted email, a CRM task, an ad audience, into the tools your team already uses. Measuring whether the fix actually worked The clearest sign that these break points are resolved isn't a higher intent-tool usage number, it's a shrinking gap between the number of accounts flagged as in-market and the number that received a genuinely personalized outreach attempt within a few days. Enterprise teams that track this specific ratio, flagged versus actually contacted with relevant context, tend to catch a regression early, before it shows up three months later as a quarter with more intent data than pipeline to show for it. FAQ Why do enterprise teams struggle with intent data more than smaller companies? Because enterprise deals involve larger buying committees and higher signal volume, both of which defeat manual triage and account-level scoring at scale. Is the fix more intent data, or something else? Something else. The fix is resolution (contact-level, not account-level), automated scoring, and system integration, not additional raw signal volume. How big is the typical enterprise buying committee? Gartner's research puts the average at 11 stakeholders, with six to ten decision-makers commonly cited for complex B2B purchases. Can this be fixed without replacing our existing ABM platform? Yes. Contact-level scoring and execution are typically layered on top of an existing account-level platform rather than replacing it. ‍ What's a realistic timeframe to see the flagged-versus-contacted ratio improve? Most teams see the ratio start moving within a few weeks of automating the scoring and routing steps, since the fix is largely operational rather than requiring new data sources. ‍ No items found. body_text: Thinking about trying RingCentral ? Or maybe you’re already using it and starting to run into roadblocks. RingCentral’s biggest strengths are its desk phone rentals, built-in video conferencing, and international local numbers. But once you start using it, you may quickly bump up against where it falls short. It has limited business texting, call recording storage, and toll-free minutes. It’s a communications platform designed for mid-market and enterprise teams, not for small businesses that need extensive text support. In this post, we’ll share RingCentral’s pros and cons in detail so that you can evaluate whether it’s right for you. We’ll also introduce you to a more flexible, modern business phone alternative designed for small and growing teams. RingCentral pros and cons at a glance Here’s a quick summary of RingCentral’s pros and cons for your reference. These pros and cons are specific to RingCentral’s business phone system RingEX. See our full RingCentral review for a detailed breakdown of features. RingCentral pros If you run a mid-market or enterprise business, RingCentral may work for you. It gives you the ability to add multiple communication modes on top of your phone. It also helps you expand into global territories and manage hundreds of team members in one place. Here are the biggest advantages that RingCentral can offer: 1. Local numbers in international countries If you’re planning to expand globally, RingCentral can support you by offering local numbers in new markets. That way, you can use a single phone system to manage communications for teams around the world. RingCentral offers local numbers in 45 countries and territories. You’ll be able to build trust with customers outside the US and Canada. You can also deliver local customer support and avoid paying international calling rates. 2. Built-in video conferencing RingCentral isn’t just a business phone system. It offers video conferencing in every plan. You can host meetings with up to 200 participants and record meetings, too. You also get end-to-end encryption of your meetings. You don’t need to get an additional Zoom or Google Meet account for your team. 3. Desk phone rentals While most modern businesses have moved on from desk phones, RingCentral still supports physical hardware. If your team hasn’t made the switch to softphones , this compatibility makes it easy to keep your current setup. RingCentral also lets you rent desk phones directly from them, but it does come at an additional cost. 4. 500+ app integrations RingCentral helps you share your call and text data wherever your team needs it. With hundreds of app integrations, your call logs plug into your existing stack. Keep in mind, RingCentral’s CRM integrations are only available in its Advanced plan and higher. Want more control over the data you share with your tools? RingCentral’s API helps you customize your integrations in detail. 5. Multiple communication add-ons Similar to its video meeting features, RingCentral offers different add-ons you can use to communicate with your customers. Set up hybrid conferencing options with RingCentral Rooms and create team-wide webinars with RingCentral Events. You don’t need separate software to bridge your physical and virtual meetings or run events across your organization. 6. Advanced multi-level IVR and call routing RingCentral supports up to 250 submenus in its auto-attendant and includes call queues with callback options and ring groups. Plus, you can route calls based on unique rules like max callers in queue. These features are best suited for businesses with high inbound call volume and dozens of different departments. 7. AI-powered conversations RingCentral offers several AI features in its platform, but what makes it unique is its AI-powered SMS capabilities. It offers SMS drafting, editing, and translation in its Advanced plan. It also provides summaries for unread SMS messages to help you catch up on what you may have missed. Keep in mind that not all of RingCentral’s AI features offer unlimited usage. For example, its AI receptionist add-on only offers 100 minutes per month to teams. If you exceed this limit, you’ll be charged 50 cents per minute for every call. RingCentral cons While RingCentral is a good option for large teams with global operations, it may not be the best fit if you’re earlier on in your journey. It limits essential communication that can hamper your growth. Here are RingCentral’s biggest drawbacks: 1. Major texting limits If your team sends a lot of customer texts, RingCentral’s limits can quickly get in the way. On its Core plan, you only get 25 outgoing messages for each user per month. The Advanced plan bumps that up to 100, and the Ultra plan to 200. That includes both SMS and MMS messages. Once you hit your monthly limit, every additional message costs $0.0119. That might not sound like much, but it adds up fast, especially if your team is in a text-heavy industry like real estate, property management, or healthcare. 2. Shared texting requires an add-on The benefit of using VoIP phones is everyone on your team has access to the same number. While this is true of calling in RingCentral, it isn’t the case with texting. You don’t get instant access to a shared team messaging inbox in your RingCentral plan. Without the ability to text as a team, it can be incredibly difficult to stay on top of customer conversations. To access shared texting, you need to purchase the Business SMS Booster add-on, which costs an additional $25 per month. Keep this in mind when you’re estimating your monthly RingCentral bill. 3. Texting registration can take months Many users have run into months-long delays when trying to complete RingCentral’s TCR registration . Some have had their applications rejected multiple times, each time for a different reason , making the whole process more frustrating than it needs to be. Others have seen their applications sit in the “review in progress” stage for weeks, with few to no updates from support. These delays can make it tough for teams to stay in touch with customers, leading to missed messages, slower response times, and a frustrating experience for everyone involved. “TCR registration took months with RingCentral, but my business was approved in just 24 hours to send texts through OpenPhone…” —– Quo user on G2 4. 90-day call recording storage limit RingCentral only stores call recordings for 90 days. After that, they’re automatically deleted. That might be fine if you just need to review a recent conversation. But it becomes a problem if you want to save important calls for training new team members, resolving long-term customer issues, or keeping records for legal or compliance reasons. Most teams don’t want to worry about a countdown every time they record a call. You need the flexibility to keep key conversations on hand for as long as they’re useful, not just for 90 days. See how RingCentral’s call recording limits work in practice. 5. Limited toll-free call minutes At first, 100 toll-free minutes each month might seem like plenty. But with RingCentral’s Core plan, that’s all you get to share across your entire team. Take a few customer calls or leave your number on your website, and suddenly, you’ve hit the limit. After that, you get charged for every additional minute. Plus, if you want an additional vanity number that’s easy to remember, there’s a one-time $30 setup fee. Between that and the minute limits, it’s one more cost to factor in as you scale your business. 6. Outdated user interface RingCentral’s phone app can feel clunky and slow to use. The layout isn’t as clean or intuitive as it could be, making simple tasks more frustrating for your team. RingCentral separates calls, texts, and voicemails into different folders, making it harder to see full conversations you have with customers. Instead of viewing everything in one thread, your team has to jump between tabs to figure out what was said and when. Compared to other business phone systems like Quo that provide a modern interface, RingCentral’s design can feel outdated. If you want to prioritize ease of use for your team, you should consider another option. 7. Frequent billing issues Past RingCentral users frequently report billing issues with the company. That includes billing for service after cancellation and overcharging customers. Take these reviews from Quo users who switched from RingCentral: “ RingCentral’s service and billing are a nightmare. Constant errors, unclear charges, and their support team is useless at best. We’ve spent countless hours trying to fix basic billing issues, and it feels like they couldn’t care less. ” — RingCentral user on G2 “ This company is only interested in ripping you off. They were charging me 950 a month for using 8 lines and would not let me out of the contract as I had sold off a portion of my business and reduced the size of my company! Even though I had been their client for over 10 years – there is no flexibility. ” — RingCentral user on G2 How Quo compares to RingCentral If you’re tired of limitations and outdated features, there’s good news — Quo is the modern business phone system you’ve been looking for. Here’s a quick look at how Quo offers a better solution to RingCentral’s drawbacks: RingCentral drawback Quo’s approach Texting limits Unlimited texting to the US and Canada on all plans Shared texting requires add-on Shared texting available by default in base plan Texting registration can take months Average registration time: 1–3 days 90-day call recording storage limit No storage limits for recordings Limited toll-free call minutes Unlimited toll-free calling to the US and Canada on all plans Outdated user interface Modern and intuitive platform design Frequent billing issues Clear, transparent pricing Unlimited texting and toll-free calling. Get access to all the SMS and MMS messages and toll-free minutes you need, even in our base plan. We don’t limit teams from using essential features like calls and texts. Communicate with your customers as much as you need. Shared numbers for calls and texts. Share conversation context for calls and texts with your team. Team members aren’t forced to ask customers repeat questions, and nothing gets lost between inboxes. Shared texting is available by default in every Quo plan for local and toll-free numbers. Smoother texting registration. Getting approved to send business texts shouldn’t take months. With Quo, formerly OpenPhone, you can complete US carrier registration in just 1–3 business days. We guide you through the entire process with clear steps right inside the Quo app, plus we offer additional US carrier registration support in our Resource Center . Modern user interface. From the moment you launch Quo, the experience is straightforward. The layout is clean, the features are easy to access, and you can start making calls and sending texts without much setup. No hidden fees or surprises. With its numerous add-ons and overage charges, RingCentral pricing can feel like it has several hidden fees. Quo’s pricing keeps everything straightforward. See what you get in each plan without worrying about keeping track of your usage. Do RingCentral’s pros outweigh the cons? RingCentral’s strengths are real: multiple communication options, global reach, 500+ integrations, and advanced call routing. For large teams with IT support, the cost is justified. But if you’re a small and growing business, a lot of those features don’t apply to you. In fact, you won’t just be overpaying for features you don’t need. You’ll be limiting access to essential features, which can hamper your growth. With SMS limits, limited call recording storage, and a clunky user interface, your business growth might stall before you get going. If these essential business phone features are important to you, you should consider looking at other platforms. We’ve done the research for you: check out our guide to the top RingCentral alternatives . FAQs Is it hard to cancel RingCentral? Several RingCentral users report that canceling is harder than expected. Plans usually run on annual contracts that auto-renew, so you often have to cancel within a specific window to avoid another term, and some users say they were still billed after requesting cancellation. Here’s an example of a user who was billed for RingCentral after canceling their subscription: “The contract has an auto-renewal feature for an additional two years, so after two years, I was opted in by contract with no notification and stuck. Then, when the contract was over, I canceled half of my lines and was assured this was done. They continue to charge me for these lines and refuse to respond to my requests for review.” — RingCentral user on G2 How does RingCentral compare to Google Voice? Google Voice is a more affordable business phone platform for teams just getting started. Pricing starts at $10 per user per month. However, it lacks business phone features like third-party integrations, texting automations, and an AI receptionist. Google Voice suits solo users and very small teams, while RingCentral fits larger teams that need the feature depth. Check out our full Google Voice vs RingCentral comparison. What team collaboration features are available in RingCentral? You can directly message team members and assign tasks with colleagues in RingCentral. You can utilize integrations with task management platforms like Asana and Jira to track your work in RingCentral’s platform.

title: Interdependence vs Codependency Explained — Talkspace
summary: Interdependence vs. codependency: Learn key signs, quick self-checks, and therapist-backed steps to build balanced bonds. Explore examples and pro help.
body_text: Key Takeaways Codependency often involves blurred boundaries, excessive self-sacrifice, and prioritizing another person’s needs over your own emotional well-being and identity. Healthy interdependence allows both people to maintain individuality, mutual respect, emotional support, and balanced decision-making within the relationship. Recognizing unhealthy relationship patterns can help you strengthen boundaries, improve communication, and build more stable, fulfilling emotional connections. One person slowly stops seeing friends, ignores their own needs, and bases their self-worth on keeping their partner happy. The partner, in turn, feels needed, relied on, and emotionally central to the relationship. This kind of imbalance is often described as codependency. In healthier relationships, both people can stay emotionally close while still maintaining boundaries, independence, and a strong sense of self. Understanding the difference between codependency and healthy interdependence can help you recognize patterns that may be affecting your relationships. Recognizing these dynamics early can help you build more balanced relationships rooted in mutual support, autonomy, and emotional well-being. Difference Between Codependency and Healthy Interdependence Healthy interdependence allows two people to stay emotionally connected without losing their individuality, while codependency often involves blurred boundaries, excessive self-sacrifice, and emotional overreliance. The table below highlights the differences between codependency and interdependence across several core relationship areas: Dimension Codependency Healthy interdependence Boundaries Difficult to maintain or communicate Clear, respected, and flexible Self-esteem Strongly tied to the partner’s approval or mood Maintained independently Reciprocity One person consistently gives more Emotional support flows both ways Decision-making One partner defers or over-accommodates Decisions are discussed collaboratively Identity Personal needs and goals become secondary Both people maintain individuality Codependency is a term commonly used to describe patterns where one person becomes overly focused on another person’s emotions, needs, or approval. According to a study in Nova Science Publishers , researchers reviewing definitions of codependency identified several recurring themes, including self-sacrifice, emotional suppression, external focusing, and attempts to manage or control another person’s behavior. Healthy interdependence looks very different. Instead of emotional dependence or emotional distance, both people support each other while maintaining their own identities, friendships, goals, and boundaries. The National Institutes of Health (NIH) guidance on social wellness describes this kind of relating as sharing feelings honestly, asking for what you need, listening without judgment, and being able to disagree respectfully. Signs Your Relationship May Be Tipping Into Codependency Do you often feel responsible for your partner's emotions, or find it hard to make decisions without checking in with them first? These are the kinds of questions worth sitting with honestly. The patterns below aren't a diagnostic checklist. They're invitations for self-reflection. Understanding what causes codependency can help you make sense of how these patterns develop in the first place. "Resisting the urge to manage a partner's emotions or make decisions in isolation requires a conscious shift from codependency to healthy interdependence. This is achieved by practicing emotional differentiation, which involves acknowledging a partner's distress without absorbing it as your own or attempting to fix it. It is essential to establish internal boundaries, reminding yourself that you are responsible for your own actions rather than the emotional reactions of another adult. Furthermore, breaking the habit of over-accommodating or taking total control requires slowing down and intentionally inviting collaborative decision-making. By maintaining a clear sense of individual identity and allowing your partner the space to navigate their own emotional experiences, you can foster a more balanced and mutually respectful relationship dynamic." - Talkspace Therapist, Reshawna Chapple, PhD, LCSW Emotional red flags Many emotional signs of codependency involve anxiety, guilt, or difficulty separating your emotions from your partner’s emotions. Some common patterns include: Feeling anxious when your partner seems upset Constantly checking whether your partner is happy with you Struggling to make decisions without reassurance Feeling responsible for fixing another person’s emotional state Ignoring your own feelings to avoid conflict Feeling guilty when prioritizing your own needs These behaviors often develop gradually. They can feel like love, loyalty, or support at first, which is one reason codependency can be difficult to recognize. Boundary red flags Difficulty maintaining boundaries is another common sign of codependency. According to NIH guidance on healthy relationships, setting limits and communicating needs clearly are important parts of emotional well-being. Boundary-related signs may include: Canceling plans regularly to accommodate your partner Feeling uncomfortable saying no Avoiding honest conversations to prevent upsetting someone Pulling away from friendships or hobbies Feeling guilty for spending time alone Accepting behavior that repeatedly crosses your limits These signs are not proof that a relationship is unhealthy. They are invitations for self-reflection and opportunities to better understand your emotional patterns. If some of these signs feel familiar, it may help to compare them with what healthy interdependency traits actually look like in everyday relationships. Traits That Define a Healthy, Interdependent Partnership Healthy interdependence allows both people to feel emotionally connected while still maintaining independence, boundaries, and mutual respect. The following interdependency traits help relationships feel supportive rather than emotionally consuming. Mutual respect and clear boundaries In healthy relationships, both people understand that emotional closeness does not require constant togetherness. Partners support each other’s individuality instead of viewing independence as rejection. "In a healthy partnership boundaries are not viewed as walls or signs of rejection. They are treated as essential tools for emotional well-being. You can hold space for your partner’s anger, sadness, or disappointment without absorbing those feelings as your own or feeling an urgent need to "fix" them." - Talkspace Therapist, Reshawna Chapple PhD, LCSW For example, one partner might spend Saturday morning with friends while the other takes time for a favorite hobby. Neither person feels threatened, guilty, or resentful. There's trust that the relationship remains secure even when both people spend time separately. Healthy boundaries also include: Respecting alone time Supporting personal goals Encouraging outside friendships Communicating honestly about needs Accepting that disagreement is normal Independent Self Esteem Identity When identity is maintained, self-worth is generated from within rather than being entirely tethered to a partner's approval or mood. Honest Communication: Both individuals feel safe using "I" statements to express limits Outside Connections: Both partners continue to invest in separate friendships, unique hobbies, and personal goals. Autonomy in Choices: While major life decisions are discussed collaboratively, neither partner feels the need to constantly defer or over-accommodate just to avoid conflict. Strong interpersonal relationships and friendships outside a romantic relationship can also support emotional well-being. Research published by the American Psychological Association found that supportive friendships are linked to better mental and physical health, greater resilience, and lower stress levels. At the same time, be careful that your reliance on friends is balanced, too; codependency in friendship is common as well. Balanced support and shared decision-making Healthy support is reciprocal. Both people can ask for help, express vulnerability, and provide emotional care without one person carrying the entire emotional burden. For example, when making a major financial or family decision, both partners participate in the conversation rather than one person automatically deferring to the other. Disagreements may still happen, but both individuals feel heard and respected during the process. Balanced relationships also tend to include: Shared emotional labor Collaborative problem-solving Honest communication Flexibility during stressful periods Mutual accountability Shifting From Codependency to Interdependence: Inner Work That Helps Moving from codependency to interdependence usually involves building self-awareness, practicing boundaries, reconnecting with your own needs, and strengthening support systems outside the relationship. Changing relationship patterns rarely happens overnight. Most people develop these habits over the years through family dynamics, attachment experiences, or previous relationships. The goal is not perfection. It is creating a healthier emotional balance over time. Self-awareness practices Self-awareness helps you notice emotional patterns before they happen automatically. Journaling can help you identify moments where you ignore your own needs, feel responsible for another person’s emotions, or avoid conflict out of fear. Helpful journaling prompts may include: What do I need emotionally right now? Do I feel safe expressing disagreement? When do I feel guilty for prioritizing myself? What situations make me abandon my own needs? Mindfulness exercises can also help you pause before reacting emotionally. Even brief daily check-ins can improve emotional awareness and communication over time. Boundary skill-building Learning to set boundaries can feel uncomfortable at first, especially if you're used to prioritizing other people’s comfort over your own needs. One helpful starting point is practicing “I” statements, such as: “I need some time to think before making a decision.” “I feel overwhelmed when I take responsibility for everything.” “I would like to spend time with friends this weekend.” You can also practice saying no in smaller situations before addressing more emotionally charged conversations. Over time, boundary-setting becomes less about conflict and more about honest communication. Expanding support systems Codependency often intensifies when one relationship becomes your primary source of emotional support, validation, identity, and connection. Reconnecting with your broader support system can help restore balance. This may include: Spending time with friends Reinvesting in hobbies Joining community groups Prioritizing physical and emotional self-care Building routines outside the relationship A simple three-step plan can help you begin: Choose one self-awareness practice to try this week. Practice one honest boundary conversation. Schedule time for a friend, hobby, or solo activity. Tracking your progress through journaling or a mental health app may help you notice small changes over time. Sometimes, self-guided efforts are enough. Other times, outside support can make the process feel more manageable and less isolating. When to Seek Professional Guidance on Relationship Patterns Many people begin exploring how to stop being codependent with professional support after noticing that relationship patterns continue affecting their emotional well-being despite repeated efforts to change them. Seeking therapy does not mean you have failed. In many cases, it means you're recognizing that certain emotional patterns are difficult to untangle alone. Signs therapy is needed A licensed therapist may help if you notice: Repeated relationship patterns that don't improve Communication breaking down consistently Emotional distress affecting sleep, work, or daily life Intense anxiety around boundaries or conflict Difficulty identifying your own needs One partner resisting all conversations about change Relationship stress can significantly affect emotional well-being. According to the Canadian Red Cross , chronic interpersonal stress is associated with increased anxiety, emotional exhaustion, and reduced psychological well-being. Therapy can provide structure, emotional support, and practical tools for changing long-standing relationship habits. Choosing the right therapist Finding the right therapist often starts with looking for someone experienced in: Relationship dynamics Attachment patterns Boundary-setting Couples therapy Emotional regulation It's also worth knowing that codependency isn't a formal psychiatric diagnosis. If you're concerned about what you're experiencing, a licensed provider can help you understand what's actually going on without applying a label that may not fit. How Talkspace Can Support Your Journey to Healthy Interdependence Building healthy interdependence in a relationship takes time, self-awareness and, often, outside support. Recognizing old patterns and learning to balance connection with independence isn't always easy to do on your own. Online therapy makes that process more accessible. Whether you're working through personal boundaries or navigating closeness as a couple, Talkspace connects you with professionals who understand relationship dynamics. Couples therapy through Talkspace gives partners a structured space to build trust and communicate more openly. Ready to take the next step? Connect with a licensed therapist at Talkspace and start building a healthier, more balanced relationship today. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) What's the main difference between codependency and interdependence? The main difference is that codependency often involves blurred boundaries and relying on another person for self-worth, while interdependence supports emotional closeness alongside independence and mutual respect. In healthy interdependence, both people can give and receive support without losing their individual identity. Can you love someone and still be codependent? Yes, you can genuinely love someone and still experience codependent relationship patterns. Codependency is not about a lack of love, but about unhealthy emotional reliance, blurred boundaries, or prioritizing another person’s needs at the expense of your own well-being. How do I start setting boundaries to avoid codependency? Start by identifying your own needs, limits, and emotions instead of automatically prioritizing someone else’s expectations or approval. Setting small, consistent boundaries, communicating them clearly, and making time for your own interests and support systems can help reduce codependent patterns over time. Does interdependence mean I never need help? No, interdependence doesn't mean avoiding help or handling everything alone. It means both people can rely on each other for support while still maintaining healthy boundaries, independence, and a strong sense of self. Is codependency a mental health disorder? Codependency isn't officially recognized as a mental health disorder in diagnostic manuals, but it describes unhealthy relationship patterns involving excessive emotional reliance and poor boundaries. These patterns can still affect emotional well-being and are often explored in therapy or relationship counseling. Sources Dear GE, Roberts CM, Lange L. Defining codependency: a thematic analysis of published definitions. In: Shohov S, ed. Advances in Psychology. Vol 34. Nova Science Publishers; 2004:189-205. https://ro.ecu.edu.au/ecuworks/7153/ . Accessed May 18, 2026. National Institutes of Health. Social wellness toolkit. https://www.nih.gov/health-information/your-healthiest-self-wellness-toolkits/social-wellness-toolkit . Accessed May 18, 2026. American Psychological Association. The science of friendship. Monitor on Psychology. https://www.apa.org/monitor/2023/06/cover-story-science-friendship . 2023 Jun 1. Accessed May 18, 2026. Canadian Red Cross. The impact of stress on your mental health. https://www.redcross.ca/blog/2020/10/the-impact-of-stress-on-your-mental-health . 2020 Oct 28. Accessed May 18, 2026. Talkspace articles are written by experienced mental health-wellness contributors ; they are grounded in scientific research and evidence-based practices. Articles are extensively reviewed by our team of clinical experts (therapists and psychiatrists of various specialties) to ensure content is accurate and on par with current industry standards. Our goal at Talkspace is to provide the most up-to-date, valuable, and objective information on mental health-related topics in order to help readers make informed decisions. Articles contain trusted third-party sources that are either directly linked to in the text or listed at the bottom to take readers directly to the source.

title: July 2026 Newsletter
summary: ZeroDev processed more than $1B in outgoing volume and 4.33M UserOps in July, alongside the launch of ZeroDev Wallet and new ecosystem integrations.
body_text: July marked another major step forward for ZeroDev. More than $1 billion in outgoing volume moved through ZeroDev during the month. It is a significant milestone on its own and could signal the beginning of many more billion-dollar months as onchain products evolve from experiments into everyday financial infrastructure. The network also executed 4.33 million UserOperations (UserOps), making July the third-largest month on record by UserOp volume. These numbers represent real product activity: more accounts being funded, more transactions being completed, and more teams making blockchain infrastructure feel like an integrated part of the product rather than a separate task for users. That same goal shaped what we shipped in July. ZeroDev expanded its account stack, went live in a new ecosystem, and helped partners turn programmable accounts into products people can use. ZeroDev’s July Network Highlights More Than $1B in Outgoing Volume ZeroDev crossed the billion-dollar mark in monthly outgoing volume, reaching more than $1 billion during July. 4.33M UserOperations Executed The ZeroDev network executed 4.33 million UserOps, making July its third-largest month on record by UserOperation volume. A More Complete Programmable Account Stack ZeroDev Wallet launched in July, bringing embedded wallet onboarding into the same platform as smart accounts, paymasters, bundlers, session keys, policies, and transaction orchestration. Product Spotlight: ZeroDev Wallet A Programmable Embedded Wallet From the First Sign-In Most embedded wallets solve the first step: helping users create and access an account. ZeroDev Wallet is built for everything that comes next. Launched on July 7, ZeroDev Wallet gives teams a smart-account-first path to embedded wallets within the ZeroDev platform. Users can sign in using familiar methods such as email, OAuth, and passkeys. Developers can then build account experiences that support: Sponsored transactions Transaction batching Scoped permissions Session keys Account recovery Automated transactions At launch, ZeroDev Wallet supports wagmi and EIP-1193-compatible transaction flows. It also works alongside ZeroDev’s smart accounts, paymasters, bundlers, and policy infrastructure, eliminating the need to assemble the account lifecycle across separate systems. The result is a cleaner product experience: familiar sign-in for users, programmable execution for developers, and one account stack that can grow with the application. Read the ZeroDev Wallet launch post Explore the ZeroDev Wallet documentation July Technical Changelog ZeroDev Wallet Brings Embedded Onboarding Into the Platform Embedded wallet onboarding now lives inside the ZeroDev platform. At launch, ZeroDev Wallet supports email, OAuth, and passkey signers, alongside a smart-account-first approach to building gasless, batched, permissioned, and automated transaction flows. ZeroDev Goes Live on Robinhood Chain Builders on Robinhood Chain can now use ZeroDev’s account infrastructure to design onboarding and transaction experiences around their products. The available capabilities include smart accounts, gas sponsorship, transaction batching, session keys, and programmable permissions. Expanded Guidance for EIP-7702 ZeroDev’s July developer content explored how EIP-7702 can bring smart-account functionality to existing externally owned account (EOA) users. The guidance covered capabilities such as transaction batching, gas sponsorship, and session keys, as well as upgrade paths that do not require users to begin with a forced wallet migration. Partner Updates From the ZeroDev Ecosystem Beezie Continues Growing on Base Beezie continued building momentum on Base with ZeroDev and expanded to Solana in July, a strong sign of the team’s growth across blockchain ecosystems. World Launches USDC Paychecks Through Virtual Accounts World launched Virtual Accounts , giving users a way to receive paychecks directly in USDC. Employers do not need to understand blockchain infrastructure, while users receive a faster path from traditional payroll into an onchain account. Vault777 Launches Its Founders Pass Vault777 launched its Founders Pass , opening pre-registration and a waitlist ahead of launch. Early participants can claim a pass, share it on X, and earn XP on the leaderboard. Vault777 is also offering up to $10,000 in launch bonuses. What ZeroDev Is Building Next The next set of ZeroDev updates will go deeper into the funding and execution layers behind modern onchain products. The team is building a new foundation for moving funds across chains, with greater flexibility around how assets arrive and what happens after they reach their destination. ZeroDev is also exploring a higher-level developer experience for translating supported financial outcomes into prepared routes and transaction data. Signing and broadcasting would remain inside the application’s existing wallet flow. The goal is straightforward: let developers begin with what the user wants to accomplish, then make the underlying infrastructure easier to compose. More updates are coming soon. Build With ZeroDev Start building onchain products with programmable accounts, embedded wallets, gas sponsorship, permissions, and transaction orchestration.
